title: Microsoft (MSFT) Raises Its Dividend 8%. Does AI Spending Change the Investment Case?
detail:
Microsoft (MSFT) Raises Its Dividend 8%. Does AI Spending Change the Investment Case?
Neha Gupta
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 2:30 PM EDT 3 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) continues to demonstrate its commitment to returning capital to shareholders even as it ramps up spending on cloud computing and artificial intelligence. On September 15, the company's board approved a quarterly dividend of $0.98 per share, representing an 8% increase from the previous quarter.

The dividend, which is payable on December 10, extends a long-standing record of dividend increases that spans over 20 years. The company has raised its dividend steadily from $1.56 a share in 2017 to $3.64 for fiscal 2026.

The strong dividend track record is supported by strong recurring cash generation. Its subscription-based software portfolio and rapidly expanding cloud business provide relatively recurring sources of revenue and cash flow. Cash from operations increased $46.8 billion to $182.9 billion for fiscal year 2026.

Microsoft Corporation (MSFT)’s Dividend Story Remains Strong Despite Mounting AI Investment Costs
AI Spending Risks

However, aggressive investment in artificial intelligence and data-center infrastructure is putting more pressure on free cash flow and could eventually constrain the pace of dividend increases and share repurchases if AI monetization fails to keep up. Concurrently, Azure and other cloud services grew 43% in the fourth quarter, underscoring strong demand for Microsoft's cloud and AI products. However, meeting that demand requires significant capital investment, which is already putting pressure on cloud margins.

The key risk is that enterprise AI adoption or AI workloads could grow more slowly than Microsoft anticipates. If demand fails to keep pace with the company's infrastructure investments, the returns on its additional data-center and GPU capacity could take longer to materialize. Such an outcome could put further pressure on free cash flow and, in turn, limit the pace at which Microsoft can return capital to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases.

Hedge Fund Positioning

The number of hedge funds holding Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT) shares declined to 273 in the second quarter from 282 in the first quarter. Nevertheless, several major institutional investors increased their exposure. Arrowstreet Capital raised its Microsoft stake by 14% to $10.31 billion, while Fisher Asset Management increased its position by 3% to $9.92 billion, according to the insider Monkey database.

Meanwhile, bearish positioning in the stock remained relatively limited with 74.45 million shares sold short as of August 31, down from 81.31 million on July 31.

The Verdict

Microsoft Corporation (NASDAQ:MSFT)'s recurring cash generation, long history of dividend increases, and growing cloud and AI demand provide important support for its shareholder-return strategy. However, the company's unprecedented AI infrastructure spending introduces a key risk: if monetization fails to keep pace with investment, margins and free cash flow could come under pressure.

This article first appeared on GuruFocus.

Microsoft (NASDAQ:MSFT) could have another lever to extend Azure growth even after its recent acceleration, with BNP Paribas arguing that higher pricing may gradually boost cloud revenue as customer contracts renew. The firm also sees a possible SpaceX (NASDAQ:SPCX) cloud-computing deal as a future catalyst, giving investors two additional ways Microsoft could strengthen an already powerful AI infrastructure story.

Warning! GuruFocus has detected 3 Warning Sign with MSFT.

Is MSFT fairly valued? Test your thesis with our free DCF calculator.

MSFT GF Value chart

BNP Paribas analyst Stefan Slowinski said Microsoft executives acknowledged that Azure pricing is moving higher, but existing contracts will not be rewritten.

Instead, pricing will be reset upon renewal, suggesting any Azure pricing benefit should feather into results gradually rather than create a material step-up in Azure growth over the near-term, Slowinski wrote.

That distinction matters because Microsoft said Azure's recent acceleration into the mid-40% growth range has not been driven materially by pricing. Instead, fleet-level efficiency improvements and continued capacity additions remain the main contributors.

For investors, that leaves pricing as a potential incremental tailwind rather than something already embedded in recent growth.

Slowinski maintains a Buy rating and $549 price target on Microsoft.

The analyst also highlighted Microsoft's continuing need for more computing capacity. Executives pushed back somewhat on reports that the company plans to expand data-center capacity to 38 gigawatts by 2032, but reiterated that Microsoft remains in catch-up mode and is continually searching for additional compute.

That is where SpaceX could enter the picture.

Microsoft declined to confirm any relationship, but Slowinski said we would not be surprised if there is a potential future announcement. SpaceX recently disclosed a new compute customer expected to spend roughly $1 billion per month starting in December, adding intrigue around Microsoft's possible involvement.

Investor Takeaway

The bigger near-term signal is Azure pricing. Investors should watch renewal cycles, cloud growth and whether higher prices begin adding to revenue without hurting demand. A confirmed SpaceX deal would provide another capacity source, but execution and economics would matter more than the headline. Microsoft also said OpenAI revenue sharing is not currently driving Azure's outperformance, reinforcing that core cloud demand remains the central piece of the thesis.

title: Is UiPath Stock Cheap Because Of What AI Might Do?
detail:
Is UiPath Stock Cheap Because Of What AI Might Do?
Trefis Team
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 3:18 PM EDT 3 min read
PATH
NOW
SPGI
SSNC
APPN
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

UiPath (PATH) has fallen about 27% from its one-month high, though it is still up 34% over three months. The stock trades at 19.5 times earnings, against an S&P 500 median of 22.6. For a software company growing faster than most of the market, that looks like a gift. The question is whether investors see an AI threat the numbers do not show yet.

Why Does UiPath Look Like A Bargain?

UiPath sells software that automates office work. Software robots repeat fixed steps, AI agents handle tasks that require judgment, and Maestro orchestrates both across the whole process. Buyers include banks, a global insurer and the Department of War, which uses UiPath for military audit work.

Revenue has grown 14.5% a year on average over three years, against an S&P 500 median of 5.8%. Of $1.72 billion in revenue over the last twelve months, $0.36 billion became free cash flow, a 5.1% yield on the stock. UiPath also holds $1.4 billion in cash and securities and no debt, about a fifth of its $7.1 billion market value.

Why Is The Market Still Wary Of UiPath?

Look further back, and the profits are young. Operating margin averaged -2.7% over the last three years, and fiscal Q2 2027 was only UiPath's fourth straight quarter of GAAP profit. So the 19.5 multiple, priced on net income, rests on a profit base still cushioned by non-operating income — trailing operating margin is just 8.9%, well below the 21% net margin the multiple implies.

The bigger worry is AI itself. On the fiscal Q2 2027 call, an analyst asked what a new AI model from one of the large labs, reportedly far better at running workflows, means for UiPath's own workflow business. The CEO also concedes the company is still testing how to price its AI agents.

None of the AI worry shows in the reported numbers yet. Operating margin did not shrink over the last twelve months versus the year before, and management raised its fiscal 2027 outlook for revenue and annual recurring revenue (ARR). If the discount is about AI, it prices a forecast, not a business that is already slipping.

Can UiPath Make AI Work For It Instead?

Management argues that UiPath's automation and AI need each other. In the CEO's view, AI models cannot learn a company's way of working on the job. Deterministic automation is cheaper and more reliable for steps that need the same result every time, and it runs without AI tokens.

Customers are buying the combination. In fiscal Q2 2027, 18 of UiPath's top 20 deals included AI. Financial firms are moving entire automation programs onto the platform, some using Test Cloud, its software-testing product.

title: MSFT Layoffs: Microsoft Cuts 268 Xbox Jobs As Gaming Reset Deepens
detail:
MSFT Layoffs: Microsoft Cuts 268 Xbox Jobs As Gaming Reset Deepens
Arnab Paul
Tue, September 22, 2026 at 12:21 PM EDT 2 min read
MSFT
Trade MSFT on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Microsoft is cutting roles across Halo Studios, first-party studios, and Xbox Game Studios management and central teams.

Microsoft has completed about three-quarters of the gaming division restructuring it announced in July.

The tech giant plans to cut about 3,200 Xbox jobs during fiscal 2027

Microsoft (MSFT) was in focus on Tuesday, after the technology giant announced another round of workforce reduction in its Xbox business, eliminating 268 roles as it moves ahead with a major restructuring of its gaming division.

MSFT shares were down about 1.3% at the time of writing.

See what 10M+ investors are talking about. Get the Stocktwits Daily Rip for what retail is watching right now, free to your inbox

Xbox Restructuring Deepens

The cuts affect Halo Studios, other first-party studios and Xbox Game Studios' management and central teams. Microsoft has now completed about three-quarters of the restructuring it announced in July, including studio sales.

"The goal is to strengthen our franchises and games by operating fewer business units, aligning groups that already work closely together, and focusing our publishing expertise," Xbox Chief Content Officer Matt Booty said in a memo Tuesday.

Microsoft Could Close Ninja Theory

As part of the reorganization, Activision will take control of World's Edge and Rare studios and will develop the next Halo game through a dedicated team separate from Call of Duty. A smaller team at Halo Studios will continue supporting existing Halo games and the community.

Microsoft is also considering closing Ninja Theory after two proposed deals to divest the studio fell through.

The latest moves are part of the broader Xbox reset announced in July. The company plans to eliminate about 3,200 Xbox roles, roughly 20% of the division, during fiscal 2027, including about 1,600 positions cut in July.

Broader Job Cuts Reported

The reductions extend beyond Xbox. According to Business Insider, Microsoft is cutting around 500 jobs in the latest round, including positions across gaming, cloud, and AI operations.

The latest layoffs follow broader company-wide cuts in July, when Microsoft announced plans to eliminate roughly 4,800 jobs, or about 2.1% of its global workforce.

Chief People Officer Amy Coleman said those reductions were concentrated largely in Microsoft's Commercial and Xbox organizations. The company also said the eliminated positions were "not being replaced by AI," although AI is changing how work is done.
